title: Wings rehearse in Nashville | 1974
content:
Wings rehearsed in Nashville, Tennessee, on 3 July 1974.

The rehearsals took place at the farm owned by songwriter Claude ‘Curly’ Putman Jr. Wings stayed at the farm, which they rented for $2,000 a week, and rehearsed in the garage.

On this day the band added ‘Go Now’ to their repertoire. The song was written by Larry Banks and Milton Bennett, and first recorded by Bessie Banks. Her version was issued as a single in 1964, and shortly afterwards it became a worldwide hit single for The Moody Blues. It topped the singles chart in the UK, and also appeared on their album The Magnificent Moodies.

Denny Laine had sung ‘Go Now’ with The Moody Blues, and was now in Wings. The band performed it on their 1973 tour of the UK, and during their Wings Over The World Tour in 1975-6. A recording from the final Wings Over The World Tour date, on 23 June 1976, at the Forum in Los Angeles, can be heard on the live album Wings Over America.

In the evening Wings, minus drummer Geoff Britton, visited the home of Johnny Cash and June Carter Cash. Roy Orbison, whom Paul McCartney knew from The Beatles’ 1963 UK tour, was also a visitor to the Cash house.
